about: Lessons about faults in generated shots. Format, uses and lifecycle: studio_platform/pitfalls.py and docs/AI-FLOWS.zh-CN.md.

entries.cause: Generated movement usually plays 1.5 to 2.5 times slower than real life, and unevenly. Words like "slowly", "gradually" or "缓缓" in the shot text make it slower still.
entries.fix: In the film editor (剪辑), raise this clip's Speed (速度): walking about 1.5x, a quick turn or crouch about 2x, and trim the still moments at its start and end. Keep it a little slower than real life. Asking for an exact number of seconds in the text does not work.
entries.assistant: edit: remove the slow words ("slowly", "gradually", "缓缓", "慢慢") from the shot text so the next take moves faster. The clip speed itself is set by the person in the film editor.

entries.cause: The moment that must be seen was sped up or trimmed together with the movement around it.
entries.fix: In the film editor, let the clip land and hold 0.6 to 1 second at normal speed after the reveal (lower its Speed or move the trim end later). Keep a reveal shot at least 2 seconds long.
entries.assistant: point

entries.cause: The voice or the words around the line ask for slow, calm speech. Speeding a voice up afterwards makes it sound stiff.
entries.fix: Describe how this person normally talks (everyday pace, rising and falling, accent) instead of "slow" or "calm"; do not add slow words around the line; do not speed the voice up afterwards. Each speaking character keeps one neutral voice sample of ordinary talking on their character card.
entries.assistant: edit: rewrite the delivery words beside the line (remove "slowly", "calmly", "softly and slowly"; say how the person talks and what they feel). Never change the spoken words themselves unless asked.

entries.cause: The place has a picture for only one direction. Shots looking another way invent their own set, so doors, furniture and fittings differ.
entries.fix: For each camera direction used in a place, make one place picture and state the fixed counts in it (how many doors, how many handles). Attach it to every shot looking that way, remake those shots' first frames, then generate again.
entries.assistant: edit: add the fixed counts and layout to the place card's description. Making pictures and generating are done by the person, and generating costs credits.

entries.cause: About one take in four swaps the whole background partway through. Push-ins and backing-away follow shots are the most prone.
entries.fix: Pick this shot's other take. If the change comes late, trim the clip's end in the film editor to before it. Making two takes per shot and keeping the clean one is the usual cure.
entries.assistant: point

entries.cause: The shot text mentions someone who is off screen (whom they look at, footsteps outside the frame), so the video draws that person in.
entries.fix: Remove every mention of people who are off screen; write the look as a direction ("looks left, out of frame"). Then pick another take or generate again.
entries.assistant: edit: rewrite the shot text without the off-screen person and with the look written as a direction.

entries.cause: An object brought in from outside the frame is not in the first frame, so the video invents its look.
entries.fix: Put the object into this shot's first frame, or do not show it being brought in during this shot.
entries.assistant: edit: change the shot so the object is already in view, or drop the moment it is brought in. Changing the first frame is done by the person.

entries.cause: Only the hand was described, so the video dresses the arm itself.
entries.fix: In every shot where an arm reaches into the frame, add one phrase with the character's fixed sleeve from their character card.
entries.assistant: edit: add the character's sleeve phrase to the shot text.

entries.cause: Some takes come out with a texture across the whole frame; another take of the same shot usually does not have it.
entries.fix: Pick this shot's other take; generate again only if every take has it.
entries.assistant: point

entries.cause: With only a first frame and words, the video decides by itself how objects move.
entries.fix: Add a last frame (same camera, only the end state changed) and check the direction in it, then generate with both first and last frame. Anything that does not need to move (a door) should stay the same in both frames.
entries.assistant: edit: write in the shot text that things which should not move stay still. The last frame is added by the person, and generating costs credits.

entries.cause: Orbits and crane moves rarely come out from words alone. Push in, pull out, a backing-away follow and a whip pan do work.
entries.fix: Split the move into two shots, each with its own first frame, or use one of the moves that work.
entries.assistant: edit: split the shot into two shots, or rewrite the move as a push in, pull out, follow or whip pan.

entries.cause: The video does not time its actions to a sound attached when generating.
entries.fix: Generate with only background sound; place the action sounds in the film editor where the picture lands.
entries.assistant: point

entries.cause: Expressions come out one size bigger than written; "smile" becomes a broad grin.
entries.fix: Do not write smile, teeth or open mouth. Write "lips pressed together, mouth corners not pulled back" and describe the brows and eyes. The first frame's expression should be one size smaller than the goal.
entries.assistant: edit: rewrite the expression words in the shot text that way.

user_words: lip sync on the wrong person
entries.cause: With several people in the frame, the others' mouths move too.
entries.fix: Say in the shot text that only the speaker's mouth moves and everyone else keeps their mouth closed.
entries.assistant: edit: add that sentence to the shot text.

entries.cause: When the video speaks the line itself it sometimes drops or mispronounces a word.
entries.fix: Pick the take that says it right. Keep key lines short and use common words.
entries.assistant: edit: offer a shorter wording of the line with common words, and change it only if the person agrees.

entries.cause: The video does not start the line at the written moment; it can start 1.5 to 4 seconds late.
entries.fix: In the film editor, trim the clip's start to about 0.3 seconds before the line begins. A late voice from off screen can stay if the picture does not depend on it.
entries.assistant: point

entries.cause: The video occasionally says a different line from the one written.
entries.fix: Pick the other take. Short lines come out right more often.
entries.assistant: point

entries.cause: The video sometimes adds its own subtitles.
entries.fix: Add "No subtitles, no text on screen." to the shot text; pick another take if it has text.
entries.assistant: edit: add that sentence to the shot text.

entries.cause: Shots used different voices for the same character, or a shot was not given the character's voice.
entries.fix: Give each speaking character one neutral sample of ordinary talking on their character card and use it in every shot; put the emotion in the delivery note beside the line, not in a new voice.
entries.assistant: point

entries.cause: Usually there are not enough credits for the job, or the service is busy.
entries.fix: Check the credits first, then wait. Do not submit the same shot again while it is waiting.
entries.assistant: point

entries.cause: An attached sound is longer than the shot.
entries.fix: Make the attached sound no longer than the shot's length, then generate again.
entries.assistant: point

entries.cause: Generation occasionally fails for reasons that have nothing to do with the shot.
entries.fix: Generate again. Making two takes per shot usually leaves at least one good one.
entries.assistant: point
